clue.text: Try and keep this — it used to drop slugs into water!

definitions.text: it used to drop slugs into water

parts.note: to have a try at something is to have a shot at it
a keep is the main tower of a castle

explanation.surface: An exclamation about some tall contraption that once dropped garden slugs into a pond, urging us to preserve it.
explanation.walkthrough: The slugs are not garden pests but lumps of molten lead, dropped from a height into water to harden into round shot.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall structure was built so molten lead fell through the air and set as balls on hitting a tank of water.

clue.text: Change underskirt

definitions.meaning: to change something's position is to move it along
a loose slip or chemise worn under a dress

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for altering or moving, and an old name for a woman's simple undergarment.

clue.text: Survive until tenth wicket?

definitions.meaning: to survive longer than another is to outlive or ... them
in cricket a batsman not dismissed until the tenth wicket falls is the final one to be dismissed, read as a two-word phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the word as OUT LAST: in cricket, a batsman who lasts until the tenth wicket falls is the last one out.
explanation.definitionFit: To survive a rival or ordeal is to endure longer than it, keep going past its end.

clue.text: Prison confines within which task must be done be done

definitions.text: within which task must be done

parts.note: doing time is slang for serving a prison sentence
confines are boundaries, and a limit is a boundary

explanation.surface: Prison walls enclose the space in which a set chore has to be finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held repeats 'be done', an OCR slip; the second pair of words plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadline or allotted period is the span of time inside which a job has to be completed.

clue.text: We have a grim register those facing the high jump may use

definitions.text: those facing the high jump may use

parts.note: a grim look is a stern one
a roll is a list or register of names

explanation.surface: We hold a stern list of names, used by those in serious trouble, facing the high jump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facing the high jump' sounds like being in trouble, but it is literal: this is a style of clearing the bar in athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: A technique in athletics high jumping, where the jumper rolls over the bar side-on, is something such jumpers may employ.

clue.text: Pole with a pistol

definitions.meaning: a long thin stick or staff
American gangster slang for a handgun

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a slender stick or staff, and in old American slang it also means a gun.

clue.text: Golden French composer

definitions.meaning: of or containing gold, chemically or poetically
Georges ..., French composer and member of Les Six

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means of gold (from Latin aurum), and it is also the surname of a twentieth-century French composer.

clue.text: Acknowledge a sound of cattle around lake

indicators.note: around says the cattle's sound sits beside the lake's letter, closing round it

parts.note: cattle low, meaning they moo
L is a standard map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone admits to hearing a single moo carrying around the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts the cattle sound against L for lake, giving L then LOW, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow a point is to grant or acknowledge it as true.

clue.text: With nothing to lose, to prorogue can a make us form new parties

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'With nothing to lose, to prorogue can a make us form new parties' is OCR-garbled ('to', 'can a make us'): PROROGUE less O anagrams to the answer, but the anagram indicator and definition cannot be fixed from the held text
annotationWithheld.clue: With nothing to lose, to prorogue can a make us form new parties

clue.text: A man with a cart shifting a raft of logs kris

indicators.note: shifting means the letters of these words move into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A man with a cart moves a raft made of logs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' rearranges AMAN plus ACART. The trailing 'kris' in the held clue is an OCR stray with no job.
explanation.definitionFit: The original catamaran was a raft of tied logs used in southern India, before the word came to mean a twin-hulled boat.

clue.text: Such a narrow area is accordingly without a motorway

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go around the motorway's

parts.note: accordingly and thus both mean therefore
M is used for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: Such a narrow strip of land lacks a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but it means outside: THUS goes round M.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a narrow neck of land joining two larger land masses.

clue.text: Possibly Turkish transport

definitions.meaning: Turkish ... is the sweet, so the word may be preceded by Turkish
a transport of joy is great pleasure or rapture

explanation.definitionFit: Being carried away with joy, in rapture, is a strong sense of pleasure.

clue.text: Drag hunt

definitions.meaning: to drag a net along the seabed
to search thoroughly through something for what is wanted

explanation.definitionFit: The word means fishing by dragging a net, and also searching widely through material.

clue.text: Push Othello, say, to make a comeback in play

parts.note: to elbow is to push or shove

indicators.note: making a comeback means the word for Othello is read in return, backwards

parts.note: Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: An actor shoves Othello back on stage for a comeback performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make a comeback' turns MOOR into ROOM. 'play' is the noun meaning free movement, not a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Play as in slack or scope means space to move freely, just as this phrase does.

clue.text: Twigged the sort of seat needed for a ala hopeless case?

definitions.text: Twigged the sort of seat needed for a ala hopeless case?

parts.words: Twigged the sort of seat needed for a ala hopeless case?
parts.note: twigged reads as made of twigs, a woven wicker seat, while a hopeless case is slang naming a woven container; 'ala' is an OCR stray

explanation.surface: Someone realises what kind of seat a hopeless person requires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twigged' seems to mean understood, but it means made from twigs, wicker. A hopeless person is a 'basket case', so the seat for one combines the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicker seat is woven from twigs, and its first word completes the slang phrase for someone hopeless.

clue.text: Saw the unions retreat

indicators.note: retreat says the letters go backwards

parts.note: the TUC, Trades Union Congress, is the federation of British trade unions

explanation.surface: The unions saw a retreat on their part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns TUC backwards. 'Saw' is the verb, to sever with a saw.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawing through wood is one way of slicing it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: President was intelligent, but finally failing the country

indicators.note: finally failing means the last letter of the word for intelligent is dropped

parts.note: intelligent and clever are synonyms
a country is a land

explanation.surface: A president was bright but at the end let the nation down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally failing' takes the R off CLEVER, leaving CLEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grover Cleveland was the 22nd and 24th President of the United States.

clue.text: Ship that blows up destroyers at anchor?

definitions.text: Ship that blows up destroyers at anchor?

parts.words: Ship that blows up destroyers at anchor?
parts.note: the destroyers are not warships but explosive devices moored at sea, which this vessel clears and detonates

explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyers' suggests warships; here they are moored mines, which destroy ships, and this vessel blows them up.
explanation.definitionFit: This naval vessel clears explosive mines, many of them anchored to the seabed.

clue.text: Ground wretch that's throwing up on the lawn

definitions.text: that's throwing up on the lawn

parts.note: ground and earth both mean soil
a worm is a contemptible person, a wretch

explanation.surface: A grovelling wretch is being sick on the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing up' sounds like vomiting; it refers to the casts this creature leaves on lawns.
explanation.definitionFit: These soil creatures push little heaps of castings up on to grass.

clue.text: Try to get people to come to one's party

definitions.text: Try to get people to come to one's party

parts.words: Try to get people to come to one's party
parts.note: reads as inviting guests to a social gathering, but the party is political and the coming is at the ballot box

explanation.walkthrough: The party is political, not social: to bring people over is to win their votes.
explanation.definitionFit: Campaigning for votes for a political party is canvassing support in a contest at the polls.

clue.text: Set papers cut up — not yours

annotationWithheld.clue: Set papers cut up — not yours

clue.text: Serious offence cutting function short

indicators.note: cutting says letters are removed from the word for function
short means the word is curtailed, its final letter lost

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A grave crime that cuts a role short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' and 'short' together take the final E off SINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave wrong, especially against moral or religious law, is a transgression.

clue.text: Moved to one side to avoid young

parts.note: to shun is to avoid
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress

explanation.surface: Someone stepped aside to keep away from a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: TED, a Teddy boy, was a young man of a 1950s British youth fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway wagons that are shunted are pushed aside on to a siding, so the word means sidelined.

clue.text: Protestant in the city sadly leaving

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the city's postcode

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: sadly means the letters of the following word are put into a disordered state

explanation.surface: A Protestant in the City is sad to be departing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' scrambles the word 'leaving', and 'in' sets the result inside the City of London's postcode; 'in the city' looks like scene-setting, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangelical churches are Protestant, so the adjective denotes a Protestant of that wing.

clue.text: Get bigger pound, where dog does this? don; mr

parts.note: to grow is to get bigger
L, from Latin libra, stands for pound sterling

explanation.surface: A dog pound grows larger, and that is where a dog snarls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like a dogs' home but gives L. The trailing 'don; mr' in the held clue is an OCR stray with no job.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog snarls with a low rumble in its throat, which is what this verb names.

clue.text: The time of day I can find an alluring woman

parts.note: asking the time of day means asking the hour

explanation.surface: At a certain time of day I can find an attractive companion.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic tradition a beautiful nymph of paradise, and by extension any voluptuous, alluring woman.

clue.text: Bile accumulates in part of the small Wilts; intestine

indicators.note: in part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Bile builds up in a section of the small intestine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wilts;' in the held clue is an OCR stray; the definition is 'small intestine'.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective relates to the ileum, the last section of the small intestine.

clue.text: Some large car taken in for maintenance

indicators.note: taken in says one word is held inside the other

parts.note: some and any are interchangeable in questions
a limo, short for limousine, is a large luxury car

explanation.surface: Part of a big car is brought into a garage for servicing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' puts the car inside the word for some. 'maintenance' is money paid to a former spouse, not car servicing.
explanation.definitionFit: Maintenance in the legal sense is the regular payment made to a former spouse after divorce.

clue.text: A rise in salary causing gossip

indicators.note: rise in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: salary is pay

explanation.surface: A pay increase sets the office tongues wagging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' sounds like a pay increase, but in a down clue it turns PAY upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To chatter or gossip noisily is to jabber, a sense of this word.

clue.text: Ardent supporter is pale when in drink

indicators.note: when in says the post is placed inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink
a pale is a stake or post, as in a paling fence

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic fan goes white when drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pale' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun meaning a fence stake.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a leading advocate or champion of a cause, after the first followers of Christ.

clue.text: Live healthily after start of diet

indicators.note: after says the healthy word follows that first letter
start of means the first letter of the word diet

parts.note: well and healthily both describe good health

explanation.surface: Lead a healthy life once a diet is begun.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside or live somewhere is to make one's home there.

clue.text: Airborne soldier, one caught circling the sea, needs emergency help

indicators.note: circling says the soldier, one and caught go round the sea

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A paratrooper captured while flying round the Mediterranean needs urgent rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' has the soldier, one and caught wrapped around the sea. The definition names the person by the help given.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained medical worker who gives urgent treatment, often in an ambulance, provides emergency aid.
